item.title: 7 ways to Create Table in Oracle SQL
item.description: Learn 7 ways to create tables in Oracle SQL, including examples and tips. Discover using the CREATE TABLE statement, the CREATE TABLE AS SELECT statement, the CREATE TABLE LIKE statement, the CREATE GLOBAL TEMPORARY TABLE statement, the CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW statement, the CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE statement, and the CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE statement. Summary of Create table in Oracle: Creating tables in Oracle SQL is a fundamental task in database management. There are several ways to create tables in Oracle, including the CREATE TABLE statement, the CREATE TABLE AS SELECT statement, the CREATE TABLE LIKE statement, the CREATE GLOBAL TEMPORARY TABLE statement, the CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW statement, the CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE statement, and the CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE statement.

item.title: Drop Table IF EXISTS in Oracle - Alternative Solutions
item.description: Learn about the best ways to drop table if exists in Oracle if it exists. Find out how to use exception handling, the “WHENEVER SQLERROR ” command, and more to drop a table in Oracle if it exists. item.title: Alternative to CONCAT_Ws in oracle SQL
item.description: Learn about the different ways to concatenate strings in Oracle, including the CONCAT and CONCAT_WS in oracle functions and the “||” operator . Discover how to concatenate strings with and without separators, and see examples using the JustLee book database. Summary of tutorial: This tutorial covers 7 different ways to concatenate strings in Oracle. It includes an introduction to concatenation in Oracle, and covers the CONCAT function and “||” operator, as well as other methods.

item.title: How to generate insert statements from existing table in Oracle SQL
item.description: This tutorial will help you to learn how to generate insert statements from existing table in Oracle SQL. Learn the different ways to do this and see examples using the JustLee book database . **Summary of tutorial post:**In this tutorial, we will discuss the various ways to generate insert statements from an existing table in Oracle SQL. We will provide examples using the JustLee book database to show how to generate insert statements using the SELECT statement, the INSERT INTO SELECT statement, and the CTAS ( CREATE TABLE AS SELECT) statement.

item.title: How to use Union in Oracle SQL
item.description: Learn how to use the Union operator in Oracle SQL to combine the results of two or more SELECT statements. This tutorial includes examples and tips for using Union in Oracle SQL with the JustLee book database and a school sample database. Introduction to Union in Oracle SQL: The Union operator in Oracle SQL is used to combine the results of two or more SELECT statements into a single result set.

item.title: How to create CHECK constraint on date in Oracle SQL
item.description: In this tutorial, we will learn about the CHECK constraint on date in Oracle SQL, including its syntax, types, and examples using the JustLee book database. Summary of CHECK constraint on date: A CHECK constraint is used to enforce a condition on one or more columns of a table in SQL. The CHECK constraint on date is used to ensure that the value in a date column meets certain conditions, such as being a valid date or falling within a specified range.

item.title: How to Create Function in Oracle SQL
item.description: Learn how to create a function in Oracle using the CREATE FUNCTION statement. This tutorial includes syntax, features, and examples using the JustLee book database. Summary of create function in Oracle: A function in Oracle is a stored program that can accept input parameters and return a value or multiple values. In this tutorial, we will learn how to create a function in Oracle using the CREATE FUNCTION statement. We will also explore the syntax and features of the create function statement, as well as provide examples using the JustLee book database.
